full_judgment:
This Rule obtained under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against an order dated 21.5.84 passed by Mr. Shamsunnahar Begum, 6th Munsif, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 105 of 1981 arising out of Title Suit No. 224 of 1979 allowing the petition of opposite party No. 3 under Order 22 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. The opposite-party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit against the petitioners and the non-contesting opposite-party Nos. 4-6 for eviction from the suit premises. In their written statement the petitioners denied the title of the opposite-party Nos. 1 and 2. A title suit being Title Suit No. 910 of 1979 is pending between the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 and the common purchaser of opposite-party No. 4, namely, Abdul Hye Howlader and others and in this suit the exchange deed of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 is under challenge. As the rights, title and interest of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 in the suit premises will be determined by the result of Title Suit No. 910 of 1979; the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 became disinterested in Title Suit No. 2234 of 1979 and allowed the said suit to be dismissed for default on 25.11.81. However on 10.12.81 the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 105 of 1981 for setting aside the order of dismissal for default dated 25.11.81 on the main ground that the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 who was the tadbirkar of the suit was ill on the date of hearing. He sent a medical certificate to his learned Advocate on the date of hearing but the learned Advocate could not file the petition for adjournment in time and so the suit was dismissed for default at 11 AM. 

 4. On 8.4.84 the opposite party No.3 filed an application under Order 22 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Miscellaneous Case No. 105 of 1981 for being added as a co-petitioner in the miscellaneous case on the averments, inter alia, that on 17.3.81 the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 transferred the entire suit property to the opposite party No.3 by a registered deed of gift delivering possession thereof and as such as an assignee of the plaintiff-opposite parties, the opposite party No.3 may be made a co-petitioner in the miscellaneous case. 

 7. Mr. Md. Zakir Hossain, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that an application under Order 22 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable only to suits and not to a miscellaneous proceedings under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 "10.-(1) In other cases of an assignment, creation or devolution of any interest during the pendency of a suit, the suit may, by leave of the Court, be continued by or against the person to or upon whom such interest has come or devolved. 

 9. It is clear that Order 22 rule 10 CPC provides for substitution in case of assignment before final order in a suit. The word "suit" has not been defined in the Code of Civil Procure, but it is well-settled that the word "suit" includes an appeal. This is also clear from Order 22 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 10. It seems however doubtful as to whether the word "suit" occurring in Order 22 rule 10 also applies to a miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed Title Suit No. 224 of 1979 against the defendant-petitioners and the opposite party Nos. 4-6 for their eviction. This suit was dismissed for default of the plaintiff-opposite parties on 25.11.81. Therefore as far as Title suit No. 224 of 1979 is concerned, it is no longer a pending suit. Order 22 rule 10 cannot apply to Title suit No. 224 of 1979 until it is restored to its file and number. 

 11. In Miscellaneous Case No. 105 of 1981, filed under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the question is whether the opposite-party Nos. 1 and 2 can satisfy the Court that there was sufficient cause for their non-appearance when the suit was called on for hearing on 25.11.81. Although section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that the procedure provided in this Code in regard to suits shall be followed as far as it can be made applicable in all proceedings in any Court of civil jurisdiction, it does not appear that a miscellaneous case filed under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a proceeding within the meaning of section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure. On the contrary it has been held by Ibrahim, J. in the case of Abdur Rahman Miji and another-Vs-Abdul Wadud Mia and another 2 PLR 287 that the expression "Proceedings" in section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure includes original matters in the nature of suits, that is, matters which originate in themselves and not those which spring up from a suit or from some other proceeding or arise in connection there-with. It has been held in the said case that an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not, therefore, a proceeding as contemplated by section 141 of the Code. 

 12. Following the ratio decidendi of the aforesaid case I also hold that a miscellaneous case filed under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code is not a "proceeding" within the meaning of section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 13. In that view of the matter Order 22 rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be attracted to a miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 14. In Miscellaneous Case No. 105 of 1981, it will be for the alleged assignors opposite-party Nos. 1 and 2 to satisfy the Court that there was sufficient cause for their non-appearance when the suit was called on for hearing. Their alleged assignee, the opposite party No. 3, will have to examine the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 or both the opposite parties as witnesses in order to substantiate the averments made in the application filed under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil procedure. Independently, the opposite party No. 3 is hardly in a position to prove the case of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as made out in the application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. From that point of view also the assignee is a redundant party in the miscellaneous case.
